p.i: nà sumpsisset, suadebat homini socer, ut ibi pernoctare, animumq; recreare vellet, &c. Iudic. 19.

Qua tempestate praesides procurabat, vir quidam à Bethlehema Iudæa, orta in finibus illis fame profectus est ad peregrinandum in agrū Moabiticum, unà cum sua coniuge, duobusq; filiis. Viri nomen erat Elimelechus, mulieris Noemi: duorum filiorū Mahalon & Chelion, Ephratæi, ex Bethlehema Iudæae. His in agrum Moabiticum profectis, ibiq; degentibus, moritur Elimelechus, uxore Noemi & duob. filiis superstitibus. Filii uxores Moabitidas duxerunt, quarū uni Orpha, alteri Rhuta nomen fuit: atq; illic circiter decem annos commorati, moriuntur & ipsi ambo, Mahalon, & Chelion. Mulier autē duobus natis & viro superstes, cum apud Moabitas agens, audivisset Iovam suis subvenisse, eisq; annonam levasse, illinc digressa, comitibus duabus nuribus, in Iudæam reverti contendit, easq; in itinere sic admonuit: Revertimini

page.notes: The first line of text is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Doubtful: the sign after "Revertimini" at the right end of the last line is a small mark I could not identify, so I have not transcribed it. The word after "levasse" is partly obscured by a ligature and I read it as "levasse". The "LXXIII." is a bare number and is written as a paragraph, not a heading, per the rules.
